purpose: Lexical rule-based baseline detector for manipulation technique tags in Spanish-language classified ads. Used as the interpretable baseline for every other checkpoint. Produces a score in [0,1] and a list of tags with evidence spans.

training_data_refs.notes: Rules are hand-authored in tools/detect_manipulation.py:21-28 (RULES list). 6 rules with regex patterns and weights 0.15-0.25.

fields.score: float in [0,1], capped sum of matched rule weights
fields.tags: array of string label ids from the 6-rule set
fields.findings: array of {tag, rationale, evidence (array of matched surface strings), weight}

known_limitations: Lexical-only: misses semantic and structural manipulation that does not match a keyword regex.
Spanish-only patterns with English fallbacks; other languages unsupported.
Word-boundary regexes (\b) are ASCII-centric; may under-match on accented characters (challenge R1-D04).
Weights are hand-tuned, not learned; no calibration against ground truth.
Always returns a score even on empty/no-rule-match text (score 0.0); abstention is by convention, not enforced.
No notion of confidence intervals; the score is a single point estimate.
risk_tier_rationale: Fully transparent (rules visible in source). Reproducible. No personal data emitted. Used only as a baseline; never as the sole decision-maker.

purpose: TF-IDF + OneVsRestClassifier(LogisticRegression) multi-label model that predicts manipulation technique tags from ad text. Trained on weak labels derived from rule-detector-v1 + metadata cues. This is the v1 ManiPsych council model.

training_data_refs.notes: NOT VERIFIED — modeling_manifest.jsonl does not exist in the sandbox. The training may have used ad_manifest.jsonl directly or a now-missing modeling subset.

input_schema.max_length: unbounded but vectorizer caps at 3000 features

fields.predicted_labels: array of string label ids (20-label v1 schema manipsych-span-v1)

output_schema.note: Label set is a superset of the 6 rule-detector labels plus 7 metadata-context labels. NOT identical to the v1 council annotation schema (which has 20 labels).

known_limitations: Training labels are weak-supervised from rule-detector-v1, NOT independently validated. Metrics measure agreement with the labelling function, not real-world performance.
TF-IDF unigrams+bigrams ignore semantic content; out-of-vocabulary ads degrade.
LogisticRegression with class_weight=balanced over-predicts rare labels.
No calibration applied; probabilities are raw sigmoid outputs (challenge R1-D06).
Spanish-only; no multilingual handle.
Trained on a single corpus collected from 5 Peruvian platforms; generalisation to other regions/languages unverified.
No held-out gold set; the 28-record 'challenge' split is the only quasi-independent evaluation, and it has only 28 records (statistically weak).
risk_tier_rationale: Weak-supervised labels mean the model is effectively learning the rule-based detector's output plus metadata correlations. Probabilities should not be interpreted as calibrated confidence. Reproducible and the artifacts are hashed, but downstream consumers must understand the labels are not gold.

metrics.note: Micro F1 is inflated by label sparsity (most labels absent per record). Subset accuracy (~0.51) is a more honest summary. Macro F1 ~0.70 indicates moderate per-label performance.

purpose: TF-IDF + OneVsRestClassifier(LogisticRegression) multi-label model trained on resolved council annotations. This is the v1 council candidate model used in the dashboards.

training_data_refs.label_source: multi-round council annotation with consensus + scientist validation + expert review round 4

input_schema.description: Free-form ad text (document text from documents.jsonl)
input_schema.max_length: unbounded but vectorizer caps at 3000 features

fields.predicted_labels: array of string label ids (20-label v1 schema manipsych-span-v1)
fields.roc_curve_micro: array of [fpr, tpr] points (downsampled to ~80 points for embedding)
fields.precision_recall_curve_micro: array of [recall, precision] points (downsampled to ~80 points)

known_limitations: Training labels are resolved council suggestions, not two-human adjudicated gold.
Metrics evaluate agreement with the council labeling function and should not be presented as independently validated human performance.
Image pixels were unavailable; image-only persuasion remains unmodeled.
Calibration status is 'uncalibrated' despite the calibration helpers in adintel.checkpoints (challenge R1-D06).
Council annotation rationale may quote ad surface text (potential indirect PII leakage).
The 28-record 'challenge' set is too small for statistically robust generalisation claims.
The council annotation pipeline may have used an external LLM (subagent IDs like 'subagent_r5_a' suggest this), which would mean ad text was sent off-host — NOT VERIFIED.
risk_tier_rationale: Trained on non-gold labels from a possibly-LLM-driven council pipeline. Strong micro-F1 (~0.90) is misleading because of label sparsity; subset accuracy is only 0.51. Used to drive the public dashboard, so its outputs are visible to analysts. Calibration is missing.
registered_in: adintel/checkpoints.py:107 (same registry slot as tfidf-ovr-v1; the council variant is a separate artifact but reuses the checkpoint_id)

challenge_split_metrics.note: Macro F1 drops to 0.47 on challenge set — meaningful generalisation gap on adversarial examples.

purpose: 17-dimension persuasive-language profile. Scores each dimension independently with a transparent signal inventory (regex + weight), returns both raw and normalised scores, abstains when signal is insufficient, and exposes a calibration hook. trust_risk and manipulation_risk are meta-dimensions that consume other scores (never a simple sum).

training_data_refs.ref: n/a (rule-based signal inventories with hand-tuned weights)
training_data_refs.notes: 17 dimensions defined in adintel/types.py:PROFILE_DIMENSIONS. Per-dimension signal lists are in adintel/profile.py:50-172. Weights are hand-tuned (e.g. urgency word=0.30, last-chance word=0.20, etc.).

fields.dimensions: dict[str, ProfileScore] with 17 entries in spec order
fields.composite_summary: dict with max_dimension, mean_dimension, n_abstained, high_risk_dimensions (FORBIDDEN: 'overall', 'universal', 'total_score', 'composite_score', 'single_score' — enforced by adintel/evidence.py:assert_no_universal_score)

per_dimension_fields.signals: list of human-readable signal names that fired

known_limitations: Rule-based signal inventories; weights are hand-tuned, not learned.
Spanish regex patterns use \b word boundaries that are ASCII-centric; may under-match on accented characters (challenge R1-D04).
Spanish Flesch readability uses [aeiouáéíóúü]+ syllable counter that over-counts diphthongs as single syllables.
trust_risk and manipulation_risk combine other dimensions with hand-set coefficients (0.45 redflag + 0.20 urgency + 0.20 emotional + 0.15 direct for manipulation_risk); not calibrated.
Confidence values (0.5-0.65 per dimension) are hand-set, not derived from data.
No held-out evaluation set; the 200-sample profile in reports/adintel/profile_sample.json is descriptive only.
Some dimensions (evidence_density, risk_reversal, social_proof) have very low corpus means (~0.001-0.01), suggesting the signal inventories may be too narrow for the actual corpus.
risk_tier_rationale: Fully transparent (signals and weights are visible in source). Abstains honestly when no signal fires. The 'no universal score' guardrail prevents the most dangerous misuse (collapsing 17 dimensions into a single manipulation score). However, the hand-tuned weights are not validated, and the Spanish regex limitations could systematically bias scores on accented text.

purpose: Multi-signal authorship / common-source analysis. Four tasks: pairwise same-source verification, closed-set attribution, open-set attribution with unknown, creative-source clustering. Includes robustness invariance tests (brand-name, slogan, disclaimer, template removal) and length-aware abstention. NEVER names a person based on model similarity.

training_data_refs.ref: n/a (similarity-based; no training in the supervised sense)
training_data_refs.notes: Uses TfidfVectorizer(char_wb, ngram_range=(4,5), max_features=2000, sublinear_tf=True) fit per-pair or per-corpus. Thresholds (SAME_SOURCE=0.55, DIFFERENT_SOURCE=0.30, OPEN_SET_UNKNOWN=0.30) are hand-set, calibrated on a small number of samples.

training_data_refs.used_for: evaluation only, not threshold calibration (challenge R1-D02)
training_data_refs.selection_bias: all 642 links are positive pairs; no negative pairs evaluated, so false-positive rate is unknown

fields.stylometry_score: float | null (cosine similarity of char-4/5-gram TF-IDF)
fields.structural_signature_score: float | null (1 - mean abs diff of punctuation/sentence/caps features)

known_limitations: Char-4/5-gram TF-IDF on short text (median 35 tokens in corpus) is sparse; even near-identical pairs only reach ~0.55-0.65 cosine similarity (challenge R1-D02).

Thresholds (0.55 / 0.30) were calibrated on a small number of hand-written samples, not on the 642 known links. Calibrated accuracy of 0.9756 on the 642 links is selection-biased (all positive pairs).
Open-set attribution uses the same threshold as pairwise verification (OPEN_SET_UNKNOWN_THRESHOLD = 0.30 = DIFFERENT_SOURCE_THRESHOLD), conflating two distinct decisions (challenge R1-D03).
No negative-pair evaluation set; false-positive rate unknown.
Council-label overlap is a SOFT signal (5% weight); the spec warns it must never be the deciding factor — verified by code.
Robustness invariance tests are approximations (one-level; do not recurse).
person_named is hardcoded False; the assert_no_person_named guard is a runtime assertion AND a test (verified).
risk_tier_rationale: Authorship / common-source analysis has the highest direct privacy risk in the package: false-positive same-source verdicts could imply coordinated inauthentic behaviour by real people. Mitigations: (a) hard person_named=False guardrail; (b) length-aware abstention; (c) thresholds set conservatively (0.55 is high for char-5-gram cosine); (d) council-overlap capped at 5% weight. However, the selection-biased evaluation (no negative pairs) means false-positive rate is unknown — this is the most important residual risk.

purpose: Outlier and novelty analysis. 11 detectors covering creative novelty, unusual technique combinations, style outliers, visual outliers, performance over/under-performers, temporal outliers, duplicates, extraction errors, metadata errors, and model errors. Every report carries comparison population, feature space, alternative explanation, and uncertainty.

training_data_refs.ref: n/a (z-score, Jaccard, hash, and pattern matching; no supervised training)
training_data_refs.notes: All detectors are unsupervised. Comparison population is the full corpus (or the input batch). No held-out evaluation set.

per_report_fields.kind: creative_novelty | unusual_technique_combination | style_outlier | visual_outlier | performance_overperformer | performance_underperformer | temporal_outlier | duplicate | extraction_error | metadata_error | model_error
per_report_fields.uncertainty: float in [0,1] (hand-set per detector: 0.0 for duplicate, 0.2-0.3 for extraction/metadata errors, 0.4-0.5 for content/style, 0.6-0.8 for visual/performance proxies)

known_limitations: 11 detectors (docstring says 'ten' — minor drift).
z-score assumes Gaussian distribution; real ad-quality scores are skewed (challenge R1-D05).
Visual outlier detector uses image_count and raw_size_bucket as proxies because the corpus has no image pixels. uncertainty=0.6 acknowledges this.
Performance over/under-performer detector uses quality_score as a PROXY because the corpus has no spend/impressions/CTR. uncertainty=0.8 acknowledges this.
Uncertainty values are hand-set per detector, not derived from data (challenge R1-D09).

No temporal outlier reports generated in the latest pipeline run (reports/adintel/outlier_summary.json shows 0 temporal_outlier entries), suggesting the detector may not be triggering as expected on this corpus.
Model-error detector depends on predictions input which is optional; if not supplied, no model-error reports are generated.
Duplicate detector uses exact-text SHA-256; near-duplicates are not caught.
risk_tier_rationale: Outlier detection is descriptive (flags for human review), not prescriptive. Every report includes an alternative_explanation, which guards against over-interpretation. The main risk is that proxies (visual, performance) are mistaken for real signals — mitigated by the high uncertainty values (0.6-0.8) and explicit 'proxy' wording in alternative_explanation.

purpose: Multi-space clustering with stability and leakage evaluation. Clusters ads in 7 spaces: persuasive (17-dim profile), semantic (TF-IDF words), rhetorical (function-word + punctuation features), visual (image-count + size bucket), multimodal (semantic + visual + rhetorical), authorial (char-5-gram TF-IDF), performance (quality_score + paid/featured/engagement).

training_data_refs.ref: n/a (MiniBatchKMeans is fit per-call; no persisted model)
training_data_refs.notes: MiniBatchKMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=3, batch_size=64). Fit on the input batch each time. Stratified sampling helper (stratified_sample) is available but the pipeline run that produced reports/adintel/clustering_summary.json used a 300-record sample.

fields.profiles: list[dict] (optional; if None, persuasive space is skipped)

per_assignment_fields.is_noise: bool (always False for MiniBatchKMeans; kept for HDBSCAN parity)

per_report_fields.resampling_consistency: float (fraction of co-clustered pairs that stay together)

known_limitations: Brand/topic leakage is near-total in 4 of 7 spaces when the sample is not stratified by platform (challenge R1-D01). The stratified_sample helper exists but the pipeline run that produced reports/adintel/clustering_summary.json still shows 100% brand leakage in semantic, rhetorical, multimodal, visual spaces.
MiniBatchKMeans is non-deterministic across major sklearn versions despite random_state=42 (n_init changed default in sklearn 1.4).
Stability ARI computation does not handle k=1 case (challenge R1-D08).

Visual and performance feature spaces use proxies (image_count, raw_size_bucket, quality_score) — clusters in these spaces are dominated by platform-specific extraction metadata, not real visual/performance differences.
Silhouette score is computed on a 2000-point subsample for performance; may be unstable for small corpora.
Cluster explanations use word-frequency which is confounded with platform (the same leakage problem).
No human-coherence validation of clusters (human_coherence_note field is always None).
risk_tier_rationale: Clustering outputs are descriptive (for analyst exploration), not prescriptive. The main risk is misinterpretation: an analyst seeing 'Cluster 0 = Locanto ads about students' may believe they found a technique cluster when in fact they found a platform cluster (the exact failure mode the spec warns against — 'treat technique presence as proof of persuasion'). The brand_leakage field surfaces this, but it requires the analyst to read it.
